              Zone Change Summary and Recommendation
Public Body: Kearns Metro Township Planning Commission         Meeting Date: July 22, 2019
Parcel ID: (various – see report)                      Current Zone: (various)          Proposed Zone: PF
Property Address: (various – see report)
Request: Rezone the properties currently owned by public entities to the PF zone as outlined in chapter 19.20 of
the zoning ordinance, adopted April 8, 2019.
Planner: Curtis Woodward
Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval


                                        PROJECT DESCRIPTION
On April 8, 2019, the Kearns Metro Township Council adopted chapter 19.20 Public Facilities Zone, as part of the
Kearns Metro Township Zoning Ordinance. The PF zone is for public and quasi-public facilities like parks, utility
buildings, civic buildings, and community centers. The PI zone is primarily for schools, churches, and public and
quasi-public places where both indoor and outdoor sports and recreational activities are held. This application
is to change the zone of several properties to the PF zone in harmony with the intent of the ordinance.

                                        EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Included in the proposed zone change to the PF zone are properties owned by Salt Lake County (parks and
recreation), Mountain States Telephone and Telegraph (now Qwest), Fire Department (SLVFSA), Kearns
Improvement District, Rocky Mountain Power, Oquirrh Recreation and Parks District (KOPFC), Taylorsville-
Bennion Improvement District, and UDOT. A more detailed list of the parcels involved is attached to this report.
Prior to today’s hearing, notices were mailed to each of the property owners regarding the potential zone
change.

                                     PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
While there are certain uses that are allowed in both the PF and PI zones, planning staff has proposed zoning
that we feel follows the general intent of the Public Facilities Zone chapter of the ordinance.

                             PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the planning commission pass the following motion:

“Move that the Planning Commission forward a recommendation for approval of rezone application 30882(A) as
proposed.”

              Zone Change Summary and Recommendation
Public Body: Kearns Metro Township Planning Commission         Meeting Date: July 22, 2019
Parcel ID: (various – see report)                      Current Zone: (various)           Proposed Zone: PI
Property Address: (various – see report)
Request: Rezone the properties currently owned by public entities to the PI zone as outlined in chapter 19.20 of
the zoning ordinance, adopted April 8, 2019.
Planner: Curtis Woodward
Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval


                                         PROJECT DESCRIPTION
On April 8, 2019, the Kearns Metro Township Council adopted chapter 19.20 Public Facilities Zone, as part of the
Kearns Metro Township Zoning Ordinance. The PF zone is for public and quasi-public facilities like parks, utility
buildings, civic buildings, and community centers. The PI zone is primarily for schools, churches, and public and
quasi-public places where both indoor and outdoor sports and recreational activities are held. This application
is to change the zone of several properties to the PF zone in harmony with the intent of the ordinance.

                                         EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Included in the proposed zone change to the PI zone are properties owned by The Church of Jesus Christ of
Latter-Day Saints, United Methodist Church, The Catholic Church, First Baptist Church, New Pilgrim Baptist
Church, Entheos Academy, Kearns Utah Congregation, Pentecostal Church, and Granite School District. A more
detailed list of the parcels involved is attached to this report. Prior to today’s hearing, notices were mailed to
each of the property owners regarding the potential zone change.

                                      PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
While there are certain uses that are allowed in both the PF and PI zones, planning staff has proposed zoning
that we feel follows the general intent of the Public Facilities Zone chapter of the ordinance.

                              PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the planning commission pass the following motion:

“Move that the Planning Commission forward a recommendation for approval of rezone application 30882(B) as
proposed.”

                     Rezone Summary and Recommendation
Public Body: Kearns Metro Township Planning Commission                  Meeting Date: July 22, 2019
Parcel ID: 20-14-232-005-0000                                           Current Zone: R-M       Proposed Zone: C-2
Property Address: 5622 S. 5600 W.
Request: Zone change from R-M to C-2.

Planner: Curtis Woodward
Planning Staff Recommendation: Recommend approval


                                             PROJECT DESCRIPTION
This is a proposal to rezone 8.19 acres of vacant land from R-M to C-2. The property is currently vacant, except for a
drainage detention basin located in the northeast corner.



                                             EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The R-M zone allows for various types of residential development, from detached single-family dwellings to apartments
(with density of up to 25 units per acre). The R-M zone also allows for some non-residential uses such as offices, medical
clinics and hospitals, and banks, but no retail sales. The C-2 zone also allows for apartments and offices, but also allows
retail uses, including mixed use developments. The property was recently sold by UDOT as surplus property.

                              SITE & VICINITY DESCRIPTION (see attached map)
         Request: Rezone from R-M to C-2                                                  File #: 30983

The site is bounded on the south by single family dwellings in an R-1-6 zone, and on the west by single family dwellings in
an R-1-7 zone. To the north is property that had been zoned C-2 when it was part of Kearns, but which was annexed into
West Valley City in 1994. To the east is 5600 West, on the other side of which are single family dwellings that face east with
no access onto 5600 West. There is currently a drainage detention basin occupying approximately .8 acres in the northeast
corner of the property. The C-2 and R-M zoning were approved in 1979 as part of a master plan by Ivory and Company to
develop 33 acres of land southwest of the intersection of 5400 S. and 5600 W. They followed through with the single-
family residential lots to the west and south of the subject property, but never built the commercial, offices, or apartments.

                                     GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS
The Official Map that was approved as part of the Kearns Township General Plan update of 2012 shows the subject
property as a “focuses area of change,” It is also located along the future bus rapid transit line along 5600 West, which is
noted as project 27 in the plan. Under the Housing section of the general plan it states: “Based on demographic data
statewide, Envision Utah suggests a mix of 60% single-family homes; 26% apartments; and 14% town homes and duplexes.”
But according to the plan, in 2000, 93% of the housing units in Kearns were detached single-family dwellings.
So the use of the property to build apartments is in harmony with the housing section of the plan. However, with 5600
West being planned as a future transit corridor, a mixed-use development that incorporates an element of commercial
either out in front of, or on the ground floor of the apartments would align better with the plan to have a BRT stop in that
area. Because the C-2 zone allows for both apartments and non-residential uses like office and retail, this zone seems most
in harmony with the general plan as a whole.



                                          NEIGHBORHOOD RESPONSE
None received as of the date of creation of this staff report.



                                     REVIEWING AGENCIES RESPONSE
AGENCY: Transportation Engineer                                         DATE:
RECOMMENDATON: Not yet received



                                 PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
The C-2 zone appears to be the best fit for a potential mixed-use, transit-oriented development on the subject property.
Staff recommends that the planning commission forward a positive recommendation to the metro council by adopting a
motion similar to the following:

“Move to recommend approval to the Kearns Metro Council of the proposed zone change from R-M to C-2 for 8.19 acres of
property at 5622 S. 5600 West as presented.”

Conversely, the planning commission could adopt an alternative motion:

“Move to recommend denial to the Kearns Metro Council of the proposed zone change from R-M to C-2 for 8.19 acres of
property at 5622 S. 5600 West as presented.”

                                                                                 Appendix



        Red – A Red area is one that has obvious potential for the future
        absorption of growth, and is likely to experience significant change
in overall area character over time. The level of stability of Red areas is
defined as follows:

        1) Major changes in land use will occur, and represent a significant
        diversion from the typical land uses in the area/corridor. Growth in
        these areas will increase, significantly raising the intensity of land
        uses. Changes in land uses may affect the majority of the area/
        corridor, and are not limited to a specific cluster.

        2) Improvements are likely to occur which will significantly alter
        the appearance, economics, or sustainability of the area/corridor.
        Improvements will have a theme, and will create a destination or
        attraction. Development of this area will likely require consolidation
        of land and coordinated planning.

        3) Mobility networks will be redesigned and will include highly
        connected, formalized, and multi-modal facilities. Public transit will
        have dedicated or fixed rights-of-way. Walkability and connectivity
        are critical to the success of the area/corridor.



        Corridor – A Corridor is a linear transportation route, including all
        parcels directly adjacent to the roadway. Corridors may have
diverse land uses and functions along their length. Corridors typically
experience change over time, responding to changing market conditions
and new approaches to land use and transportation planning. Because of
their limited access and impact on adjacent land uses, corridors considered
here do not include highways, rail corridors, or other high-speed limited
access roads.

        1) Changes occur with some frequency along important corridors.
        Land uses at important nodes, usually where two major corridors
        intersect, will intensify and absorb significant growth in the
        community. Focusing growth in centers along corridors can create

27. Transit Improvement: 5600                                                Appendix


West Bus Rapid Transit
Project Category
Infrastructure.

Location
Mountain View Corridor near 5600 West.

Objective
Pursue and support a bus rapid transit (BRT) element for the Mountain
View Corridor on 5600 West to provide service to Kearns residents.

Potential Stakeholders
Salt Lake County, Kearns Township, WFRC, West Jordan City, West Valley
City, UTA, and UDOT.

Recommendations
            Coordinate with UTA to study the viability of a BRT line along
            5600 West, and become active partners in the planning
            process. Consider potential BRT station locations in Kearns,
            and promote transit-supportive land uses, higher density
            development, and enhanced pedestrian infrastructure in those
            locations.

Timeline
Mid term.

Project added July 2009.

               Subdivision Summary and Recommendation
Public Body: Kearns Metro Township Planning Commission          Meeting Date: July 22, 2019
Parcel ID: 20-13-402-068-0000                             Current Zone: R-1-6
Property Address: 5928 S. Park Wood Drive
Request: Approval of the final subdivision plat (39 lots)

Planner: Curtis Woodward
Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval
Applicant Name: Dan Cloward


                                         PROJECT DESCRIPTION
This the final subdivision plat for the amended Parkwood Estates subdivision application on the surplus Kearns
Oquirrh Park Service District parcel. An exception was previously granted for more than 24 lots on the cul-de-sac
(“Jaycie Drive” on the attached plan) based on community members did not wanting Park Wood Drive to be a
through-street, nor be extended to create a cul-de-sac. The final plat incorporates what had previously been lot
32 of the previous plat as now being 7 additional lots, which amendment has been approved by the Mayor.

Final engineering and surveying reviews have been approved, and most of the public improvements have been
installed and inspected, with the remaining improvements having been bonded for by the applicant.

The staff suggests the following potential motion:

Motion to approve the final plat of the Parkwood Estates Subdivision as reviewed and approved by the County
